# graph-manager: the sandbox tools volume (engine + provider CLIs, mounted read-only) (KAN-88)

## What to build

A sandbox container runs a user-chosen image that only needs `node` (20+) and `git`. The engine and the provider CLIs (`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `qwen`) come from a **tools folder** that graph-manager fills and every sandbox mounts read-only at `/opt/gm-tools`:

```
<tools>/VERSION                          # written last; filling is skipped when it matches
<tools>/graph-execution/package.json     # the engine package: package.json, dist/, skills/, README.md
<tools>/graph-execution/dist/cli.js
<tools>/graph-execution/node_modules/…   # its production dependencies (transitive), flat
<tools>/bin/graph-execution              # #!/bin/sh wrapper → node ../graph-execution/dist/cli.js
<tools>/bin/claude, codex, …             # wrappers for the provider CLIs found on graph-manager's PATH
<tools>/lib/<name>/…                     # the copied provider CLI packages / install folders
```

Where the tools live depends on where graph-manager runs (the `Sandboxes` service in `src/server/sandbox.ts` already knows `self`, graph-manager's own container from `docker.inspectSelf()`, after `init()`):

- **In Docker** (`self` set): the folder is `config.sandboxToolsDir ?? "/opt/gm-tools"`, which must be a Docker volume mount of graph-manager's own container (compose mounts the `gm-tools` volume there; a later slice adds that). The sandbox mount is `{ Type: "volume", Source: <that mount's Name>, Target: "/opt/gm-tools", ReadOnly: true }`. If no such mount exists in `self.Mounts`, sandboxes are unavailable with the reason `mount the gm-tools volume at /opt/gm-tools in graph-manager's container (see docker-compose.yml)`. If the mount is a bind, use `{ Type: "bind", Source: <its Source>, … }`.
- **Outside Docker** (`self` undefined): the folder is `config.sandboxToolsDir ?? <dataDir>/sandbox-tools`, bind-mounted: `{ Type: "bind", Source: <folder>, Target: "/opt/gm-tools", ReadOnly: true }`.

This slice fills the folder in `Sandboxes.init()` (the `prepareTools()` hook) and exposes `Sandboxes.toolsMount()` for the start slice. Spec: `docs/prd/sandboxes.md` (Decisions: "The engine and the provider CLIs come from a tools volume"; Requirements → startup, second sub-bullet).

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` (whole file) — `Sandboxes` with `opts.config`, `docker`, `self`, `init()` (ping → inspectSelf → network → `prepareTools()` → available), `status()`, `defaultImage()`. Replace the `prepareTools()` stub.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.ts` — `ContainerInfo.Mounts` (`Type`, `Name?`, `Source`, `Destination`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` — `Config.graphExecutionBin` (an absolute `<engine package>/dist/cli.js` in a normal install, `defaultGraphExecutionBin()`), `Config.sandboxToolsDir?`, `Config.dataDir`.
- `packages/graph-execution/package.json` — `dependencies` (commander, execa, ink, ink-spinner, react, zod) and `files` (`dist`, `skills`, `README.md`).
- `apps/graph-manager/Dockerfile` (lines 17-40) — in the image the engine is `/app/packages/graph-execution` with hoisted deps in `/app/node_modules` (npm workspaces; `node_modules/graph-execution` is a symlink to the package), and `claude` is installed with `npm install -g` (a `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code` package; on other machines `claude` can be a native install such as `/opt/claude-code/bin/claude`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts` (lines 121-129) — `writeGraphExecutionShim`: how a `#!/bin/sh` wrapper is written (`mode: 0o755` + `chmodSync`).
- `apps/graph-manager/package.json` — `version` (0.1.0).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.test.ts` — existing tests of `Sandboxes` with the fake Docker (`startFakeDocker` from `../../scripts/fake-docker.mjs`, options `self`, `exec`).

## Patterns to follow

```ts
// terminals.ts:122-128 — a sh wrapper
writeFileSync(file, `#!/bin/sh\nexec node ${JSON.stringify(bin)} "$@"\n`, { mode: 0o755 });
chmodSync(file, 0o755);
```

Wrappers in the tools folder must work from any mount point (the fake Docker runs them on the host from the real folder), so they locate themselves:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
d=$(dirname "$0")
exec node "$d/../graph-execution/dist/cli.js" "$@"
```

and for a copied CLI: `exec "$d/../lib/claude/<relative path of its entry>" "$@"` (or `exec node "$d/../lib/<name>/<entry.js>" "$@"` when the entry is a `.js` / `.mjs` / `.cjs` file).

Copy with `cp(src, dest, { recursive: true, dereference: true })` from `node:fs/promises` (dereference: workspace and global installs are symlinks).

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-tools.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `export const TOOLS_TARGET = "/opt/gm-tools";`
  - `export const PROVIDER_CLIS = ["claude", "codex", "opencode", "qwen"] as const;`
  - `export function toolsVersion(gmVersion: string, engineDir: string): string` — `${gmVersion} ${enginePackageJson.version} ${mtimeMs of <engineDir>/dist/cli.js}` (so a rebuilt engine refreshes the tools in development).
  - `export function engineDirOf(bin: string): string | undefined` — for an absolute `…/dist/cli.js`, the folder two levels up when it has a `package.json` named `graph-execution`; else undefined.
  - `export async function copyEngine(engineDir: string, dest: string): Promise<void>` — copies `package.json`, `dist/`, and `skills/` + `README.md` when present, into `dest`; then copies the production dependency closure into `dest/node_modules`:
    - queue `[name, fromDir]` starting with every key of `dependencies` (and `optionalDependencies`) of `engineDir/package.json`, `fromDir = realpath(engineDir)`;
    - resolve a name by walking up from `fromDir`: the first `<dir>/node_modules/<name>/package.json` that exists (scoped names `@a/b` work the same);
    - each name is placed once, at `dest/node_modules/<name>` (flat; the package's own nested `node_modules`, if any, comes along with the copy); enqueue its `dependencies` + `optionalDependencies` resolved from its real dir;
    - a missing optional dependency is skipped; a missing required one throws `Error("cannot find <name> for the sandbox tools")`.
  - `export async function copyProviderClis(dest: string, pathEnv = process.env.PATH ?? ""): Promise<string[]>` — for each of `PROVIDER_CLIS` found on `pathEnv` (first executable match), `realpath` it, then:
    - if the real path is inside a `node_modules/<pkg>` folder: copy that package root (the nearest ancestor with a `package.json` directly under a `node_modules` folder, scoped-aware) to `dest/lib/<cli>/`, and write `dest/bin/<cli>` executing the entry relative to it (with `node` for `.js/.mjs/.cjs`); the package's own dependencies are resolved the same way as for the engine and copied into `dest/lib/<cli>/node_modules`;
    - else if the real file's folder is named `bin`: copy that folder's parent (the install root, e.g. `/opt/claude-code`) to `dest/lib/<cli>/` and wrap `lib/<cli>/bin/<file>`;
    - else copy the single file to `dest/lib/<cli>/<file>` and wrap it.
    Returns the names copied.
  - `export async function fillTools(dir: string, opts: { engineDir: string; gmVersion: string; pathEnv?: string; log?: (l: string) => void }): Promise<"fresh" | "filled">` — when `<dir>/VERSION` equals `toolsVersion(...)`, return `"fresh"`. Else build everything in `<dir>/.next-<random>` (engine to `.next/graph-execution`, wrappers to `.next/bin`, CLIs to `.next/lib`), remove the old `graph-execution`, `bin`, `lib` entries of `dir`, rename the three new ones into `dir`, remove `.next-*`, then write `VERSION` (last, via `.tmp` + rename). `mkdir -p dir` first. Logs `sandbox tools: copied graph-execution, claude` etc.
- **GOTCHA**: never follow `node_modules/graph-execution` back into the monorepo root `node_modules` (it is the engine itself; it is not one of its own dependencies, so the closure above never asks for it).
- **GOTCHA**: `dist/cli.js` must be executable is not required (wrappers use `node`).
- **GOTCHA**: Windows: the sandbox feature is POSIX only; `fillTools` may assume `/bin/sh`.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `toolsDir(): string` — `config.sandboxToolsDir ?? (this.self ? TOOLS_TARGET : path.join(config.dataDir, "sandbox-tools"))`.
  - `toolsMount(): { Type: "bind" | "volume"; Source: string; Target: string; ReadOnly: true } | undefined` — as described above; set during init.
  - `prepareTools()`:
    1. `engineDirOf(config.graphExecutionBin)` undefined → reason `the graph-execution engine was not found next to graph-manager (GM_GRAPH_EXECUTION_BIN=<bin>)`.
    2. In Docker: find `self.Mounts` entry with `Destination === toolsDir()`; none → the reason above (`mount the gm-tools volume at /opt/gm-tools …`).
    3. `await fillTools(toolsDir(), { engineDir, gmVersion })` — errors become `cannot prepare the sandbox tools: <message>`.
    4. set `this.mount` and return undefined.
  - `gmVersion` read once from `apps/graph-manager/package.json` via `JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../package.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")).version` (works from `src/server` and `dist/server`).
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck -w graph-manager`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-tools.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** (needs the built engine: `const BIN = defaultGraphExecutionBin(); const built = existsSync(BIN);` and `it.skipIf(!built)`, as in `routes/runs.test.ts:15-18`):
  - `fillTools(tmp, { engineDir: engineDirOf(BIN)!, gmVersion: "t", pathEnv: "" })` → `"filled"`; `<tmp>/bin/graph-execution --version` (run with execa, `env: { PATH: process.env.PATH }`) prints the engine version; `<tmp>/graph-execution/node_modules/zod/package.json` and `…/commander/package.json` exist; `VERSION` exists; a second call returns `"fresh"` and does not touch the files (mtime of `bin/graph-execution` unchanged).
  - Running `node <tmp>/graph-execution/dist/cli.js --version` from a temp cwd OUTSIDE the repo (`cwd: os.tmpdir()`) works: proves the deps are self-contained.
  - A fake provider CLI: in a temp dir create `fakebin/claude` as a symlink to `pkgs/node_modules/@x/claude/cli.js` (with `package.json` `{ "name": "@x/claude", "bin": { "claude": "cli.js" } }` and `cli.js` printing `claude-ok`); `copyProviderClis(dest, <fakebin>)` → `["claude"]`, and `dest/bin/claude` prints `claude-ok`. A plain executable file `fakebin/codex` (a `#!/bin/sh echo codex-ok` script) is copied as a single file and its wrapper prints `codex-ok`.
  - `Sandboxes` with the fake Docker and no `self`: `status()` available; `toolsMount()` is `{ Type: "bind", Source: <dataDir>/sandbox-tools, Target: "/opt/gm-tools", ReadOnly: true }`; the folder has `bin/graph-execution`.
  - `Sandboxes` with `self: { id: os.hostname(), mounts: [] }` (set `process.env.HOSTNAME`, restore it after) → `available: false`, reason contains `mount the gm-tools volume`. With `self.mounts: [{ Type: "volume", Name: "gm-tools", Source: "/var/lib/docker/volumes/gm-tools/_data", Destination: <tmp tools dir>, RW: true }]` and `config.sandboxToolsDir: <tmp tools dir>` → available, `toolsMount()` is `{ Type: "volume", Source: "gm-tools", Target: "/opt/gm-tools", ReadOnly: true }`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After `init()`, the tools folder holds the engine with its production dependencies and a `bin/graph-execution` wrapper that runs anywhere; provider CLIs on PATH are copied with wrappers.
- [ ] The copy is skipped when `VERSION` matches.
- [ ] `toolsMount()` gives the read-only mount for sandboxes (volume in Docker, bind outside).
- [ ] In Docker without the tools volume mounted, `status()` is unavailable with an actionable reason.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm run build -w graph-execution && npm test -w graph-manager -- sandbox`

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- sandbox
npm test
```
